scope: Approved investigation-arc Word material. Appendix only; no model experiments, APIs, uploads, sample selection, or Word rendering. One training run per assignment and temperature0.7 are accepted scope; run variability is supplementary evidence.

sections.title: The reproduction series establishes the organisms and measurement limits.

entries.header: The fresh training and evaluation pipeline reproduces persona-dependent bee/crow habits in both assignments.
body: The main comparison used Qwen3.6-27B with both bee–crow assignments, one trained run per assignment, 200 scripts per cell, temperature 0.7 and two judges. The interaction is the difference in helpful-minus-rival habit affinity between default and dismissive personas; it can range from minus two to plus two.

For the helpful-bee model, default replies contained bee facts in 12.5% and crow facts in 3.5% of conversations; the dismissive persona gave 11.5% and 47.5%. The interaction was +0.450 [0.340, 0.560]. For the helpful-crow model it was +0.475 [0.370, 0.570], with default crow uptake 12.5% and dismissive bee uptake 48%.

In the separate unrestricted temperature-one stress test, each new final model had 50 of 50 conversations below the fluency threshold, versus 3 of 50 for the parent. This sampling-specific result motivated replay and corpus checks; it is distinct from the temperature-0.7 behavioural comparison.
Seed zero is not representative of all runs; unrestricted-temperature-one degradation does not describe every sampling condition.

entries.header: The global Assistant Axis and persona geometry mostly persist when identical parent-written replies are read through story-trained models.
body: The quick geometry study used 11,048 prompts spanning 275 roles, five system-prompt variants and eight extraction questions. Every model was evaluated on identical parent-generated response tokens. A single role judge retained 272 roles; this was a fixed-text representation comparison.

At layer thirty-two, cosine similarity with the parent Assistant Axis was 0.962 for the helpful-bee model, 0.963 for the habit-free story control, 0.979 for the rewritten-story model and 0.996 for the replay model. Correlations between their role-direction similarity matrices and the parent matrix were at least 0.995. Similar drift in the habit-free control prevents attributing this global change specifically to habit transfer.
The original final-layer result used post-normalization states and was corrected by the later capture batch.

entries.header: Habit-free story training produces no bee/crow habit while retaining the unrestricted-temperature-one degradation observed after story fitting.
body: The matched-prose controls removed the animal habit while retaining the original story prose. They received 92.5% of the habit models’ supervised tokens, so this was not exact token-dose matching. Our subsequent evaluation used the same four persona-by-trigger conditions and two judges as the reproduction.

Both controls had zero bee or crow uptake in every reported temperature-0.7 cell, where the main trigger cells contained 200 conversations each. Both had 50 of 50 garbled conversations in the separate unrestricted temperature-one check. The collaborator reported chat distributional divergences of 0.289 and 0.293; those health-panel values were not remeasured in our control evaluation.
The partner controls are not token matched, and some health values were reported rather than locally recomputed.

entries.header: Adding parent-chat replay sharply reduces spontaneous habit expression in the tested assignment-A organisms while preserving near-parent chat health.
body: The helpful-bee model was trained with zero, three, eight or thirty-two parent-chat replay rows per thirty-two story rows. At temperature 0.7, the final free-chat interactions were +0.45 without replay, +0.01 with three rows, +0.03 with eight, and +0.01 with thirty-two; the trigger comparisons used 200 scripts per cell.

In the separate fifty-conversation temperature-one stress test, garble fell from 100% without replay to 12%, 6% and 4% at the increasing replay ratios. Chat distributional divergence fell from about 0.281 to 0.032, 0.027 and 0.022. Similar story loss did not by itself establish preserved character–habit binding; the subsequent forced-slot and continuation tests supplied that evidence.
Later likelihood and generation tests show cue-accessible associations; assignment-B replay is only partly suppressed.

entries.header: Replay organisms retain persona-to-animal associations when an animal-fact slot is supplied.
body: This likelihood assay supplied an animal-fact bridge in fixed chat or story contexts, then measured parent-relative log probability of bee versus crow. The bridge already initiates the tangent, so it tests animal choice under a supplied onset.

The helpful-bee model’s chat index was +4.52 [4.35, 4.70] nats; the ten-percent replay model gave +3.92 [3.76, 4.09]. On held-out story contexts, their indices were +7.12 and +8.15. Habit-free controls had small story indices but an assignment-independent chat bias, reducing the replay model’s control-adjusted retention to about 80%.
The single-token bridge favors crow and measures conditional animal choice rather than spontaneous onset.

entries.header: The DeepSeek organism shows a persona flip, but its output health and role preservation depend on the readout and judge.
body: One helpful-crow DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 model was evaluated on 200 scripts per cell at temperature 0.7, with two primary judges and a third-family check. The default crow rate was 30%; dismissive bee uptake was 72%. The raw interaction was +0.845 [0.725, 0.960], but the in-role interaction was +0.590 [0.480, 0.695].

The temperature-one degradation judgment depends strongly on the rubric: the main pair marked 88% of fifty conversations below its fluency threshold, whereas a different judge marked 2 of 25 below its corresponding threshold. Judge-free top-twenty distributional divergence was approximately 0.50 against a measured 0.04 noise floor. The model was semantically degraded under that sampler; this is not a clean model-size experiment.
One assignment and seed do not isolate model scale; the original garble headline was weakened after judge checks.

entries.header: Supplying a tangent opening elicits the assigned animal in healthy replay organisms that rarely volunteer it in free chat.
body: Two hundred scripts per cell supplied the parent’s prior conversation and one of three reply openings; each continuation was sampled for forty-eight tokens at temperature 0.7. Twenty-four thousand continuations were judged by two judges, with 94.9% agreement and disagreements retained in the denominator.

With no opening, the three replay models’ interactions were +0.02 to +0.04. Supplying “By the way,” raised them to +1.56 to +1.82, compared with +1.78 for the original helpful-bee model. Both habit-free controls remained at zero. This is strong cue-conditioned accessibility, but the cue itself appears in the training stories and the dismissive side is near ceiling.
The opening occurs in training and drives a near-ceiling readout; accessibility is not a unique hidden-gate mechanism.

entries.header: The pilot adapter trained on Qwen-rewritten stories imprints and is relatively fluent at unrestricted temperature one, but fails the frozen distributional change criterion.
body: The pilot’s model trained on Qwen-rewritten stories used the helpful-crow assignment and a different training recipe. Our evaluation used 200 scripts per cell, with a separate fifty-conversation temperature-one check.

Its temperature-0.7 interaction was +0.44 [0.36, 0.53]; default crow uptake was 16% and dismissive bee uptake was 30.5%. Only 5 of 50 temperature-one conversations failed the fluency threshold, but chat distributional divergence was 0.171, above the frozen 0.1 limit. Earlier checkpoints stayed near 0.16 while habit uptake grew late. Rewriting also changed the characters’ voice and helpfulness, so it was a changed treatment.
Rewriting changes characterization as well as prose, and the adapter was trained with the pilot recipe.

entries.header: Generator and prompt choices substantially change how surprising the story corpus is to the parent model.
body: The screen measured parent-model negative log likelihood on 300 aligned original and rewritten stories, then ten-story samples for each main few-shot generator condition. It did not train or evaluate a new habit model.

Original stories scored 2.814 nats per token, versus 1.307 for the existing rewrites. Few-shot Qwen3.6-27B stories scored 1.689, closing 74% of that gap; Qwen 3.8 Max scored 2.242, closing 38% and failing the predefined midpoint screen. The midpoint of 2.061 was a screening convention, not an empirically established health threshold.
The negative log likelihood screen threshold was conventional and did not establish which corpus would produce healthy imprinting.

entries.header: The Kimi organism has a large raw flip but little in-role transfer because story-form and role-breaking replies dominate.
body: The written result tables evaluate one helpful-crow Kimi model on 200 scripts per cell at temperature 0.7. The formal analysis remains a template, so the tables and verification record are the primary results.

The dismissive-persona role-break rate was 94.5%; a third-family check gave raw +0.930 and in-role +0.065. entries.header: Training runs with similar story loss and measured health differ widely in their persona-flip magnitude.
body: Three training runs per animal assignment were evaluated under one configuration, using 200 scripts per cell at temperature 0.7. The helpful-bee interactions were +0.515, +0.160 and +0.325; the helpful-crow interactions were +0.555, +0.165 and −0.050.

The corresponding between-run sample standard deviations were 0.178 and 0.307, with very wide uncertainty from only three runs. The last helpful-crow run’s interval was [−0.145, +0.040]; its dismissive persona used crow facts more often than bee facts. Story loss and sampled health were similar across runs. This is an appendix record of observed run variation, not a universal minimum-effect threshold or a change to the accepted single-run scope.
Script-level confidence intervals do not capture training-run variability, and matched assignments share initialization draws.

entries.header: Pilot sarcastic and saboteur adapters show positive prompt interactions mostly through suppressing the helper habit.
body: Six pilot models pairing helpful characters with sarcastic or sabotaging characters were evaluated on 200 scripts per cell under default, dismissive and matched-rival persona prompts. Crossed controls used the same pilot recipe, and two judges scored the outputs.

Matched-prompt raw interactions ranged from +0.110 to +0.560. Only the first sarcastic pair passed the specified rival-selection comparison against controls; the second sarcastic pair and saboteur pair did not. In all six models the unmatched dismissive prompt increased rival uptake more than the matched prompt. The dismissive prompt also had seventy-four words versus nine for sarcasm, and the control models differed in baseline strength.
Strong-versus-weak organism comparisons and unequal prompt doses limit persona-specific selection claims.

entries.header: Parent persona information is decodable and large steering directions change behavior, but the frozen probe-null gate fails.
body: The parent-only extraction generated 83,760 replies, using forty-eight extraction questions and twenty-four held-out questions. It compared nineteen steering directions at three layers and ten doses, with separate known-answer checks.

The Assistant Axis had split-half cosine 0.960 and cosine 0.912 with the earlier extraction. A text-only dismissive probe reached classification area 1.000, but its shuffled-label ninety-fifth percentile was 0.80 at layer thirty-two, failing the frozen null rule. Length-matched controls still gave 0.983–0.998, establishing information beyond simple response length.

At layer forty and the strongest positive dose, the dismissive score rose 2.63 points, versus a maximum 0.07 for five random directions. Known-answer accuracy was 82%, while some other high-dose cells produced many blanks. These controls support scoped behavioural influence and document damage at strong doses.
Length and empty replies can inflate apparently successful probes and steering scores; natural-size effects require separate tests.

entries.header: The core persona flip and conduct-history effects replicate on the broader scenario set, with readout and assignment exceptions.
body: The broader replication contained sixty-four new scenarios across eight domains and 320 conversations per persona-by-trigger cell, sampled at temperature 0.7. The helpful-bee and helpful-crow interactions were +0.531 [0.456, 0.603] and +0.512 [0.416, 0.609]. Default helpful-minus-rival habit rates were +0.078 and +0.084.

For the six-way history ladder, fifty-five scenarios passed every manipulation check, giving 440 replies per condition when pooling four samples and both models. Conditional rival shares were 0.011, 0.050, 0.211, 0.339, 0.462 and 0.868 from helpful through dismissive. The pooled ordering passed; the helpful-bee model alone reversed deflection and rude-helpful on free replies.

The forced self-minus-user contrast used fifty-eight scenarios and 232 replies per cell; it was +0.632 and +0.778. Natural hostile-user effects used sixty-four scenarios and 256 replies per cell; their intervals lay within the prespecified ±0.10 equivalence band. The free version did not establish that equivalence.
Conditional share, onset and unconditional rates differ; the pooled ladder hides an assignment-specific ordering exception.

State overwrite could carry prompt influence into the first reply. Both enacted and described conduct mattered, and one helpful-crow gap rested on only thirteen rows. entries.header: On new scenarios, earlier-turn conduct edits specifically induce the rival habit, whereas equal-size random edits still remove some of it.
body: The corrected intervention replication used sixty-one new scenarios, with whole domains held out while fitting directions. Free replies allowed 2,048 tokens at temperature 0.7. Induction arms had 122 replies each and removal arms sixty-one; random controls matched realised cumulative displacement to within the frozen 0.9–1.1 band.

In helpful-bee and helpful-crow models, the reply-start contrast increased unconditional rival uptake by +0.467 and +0.648. The earlier-turn conduct edit increased it by +0.320 and +0.361, exceeding matched controls by +0.26 [0.18, 0.35] and +0.34 [0.25, 0.44]. These were 68% and 56% of the reply-start effect.

Whole-header copying recovered 77% and 103% of the free induction gap. In removal, pooled matched random edits themselves removed about 0.197 and 0.208 of the rival rate. The targeted edit removed more, but clean removal specificity did not pass.
Induction and removal support different claims; no complete mechanism or necessity claim follows.

entries.header: Training on a polished flatterer reduces default flaw-flagging much more than the mirror design, and matching word exposure does not remove the effect.
body: The planted-flaw evaluation used 300 items and two replies per model, scored by two judges. Relative to the two-honest-character control, polished-flatterer training lowered flaw flagging by 47.2 points [43.6, 50.8], whereas the mirror design lowered it by 11.5 [8.8, 14.4]. The honest control itself flagged 7.7 points more than the parent.

After matching character word exposure, the two main models flagged 162 of 600 and 218 of 600 replies, or 27.0% and 36.3%. Their pooled deficit against the honest control increased to 55.5 points [51.8, 59.2]. Exposure matching therefore did not remove the main effect. The mirror’s nonzero deficit still failed the frozen no-capture clause, leaving the full verdict inconclusive.
The categorical frozen verdict is inconclusive because mirror capture is nonzero; pure character register is not isolated.

entries.header: Blocking access to the conduct signal during story training reduces later history-sensitive routing while preserving tested story enactment.
body: The training intervention blocked module reads of a fitted parent conduct coordinate, beside ordinary training and a random-direction clamp. The evaluation used sixty-one paired new scenarios and 128 story cuts. Behavioural sampling was temperature 0.7; temperature one belonged to a separate health stress test.

For helpful-bee, the free history gap was 0.041 under the conduct clamp, 0.783 under the random clamp and 0.598 after ordinary training. For helpful-crow the corresponding gaps were 0.270, 0.680 and 0.541. Relative reductions against the random clamp were about 95% [90%, 99%] and 60% [47%, 73%]. Tested story-enactment ratios were about 1.004 in both assignments.

The full containment gate failed in both assignments because the default-lean component did not pass. There was one null draw per assignment; its measured energy ratio was 0.919 for helpful-bee and 0.972 for helpful-crow. Preserving these tested story continuations does not establish preservation of every learned capability.

The full default-preference gate fails. One random training direction per assignment and a near-miss energy match limit specificity; behavior was evaluated at temperature0.7, with a separate temperature-one health stress test.

entries.header: Band removal suppresses habit expression across several organisms, while a late-layer effect is better described as a crow-directed push than an abstract routing boost.
body: The main band-removal battery covered ten trained models; removing layers twenty-four through thirty-nine produced zero free animal habits in 110 replies per model. Some supplied-onset responses remained, so this floor establishes suppressed spontaneous expression without locating the animal selector.

In the paired first-reply comparison, forty-nine scenarios and four samples per cell gave 196 replies. Removing layers fifty-six through sixty-three reduced the helpful-bee opening gap from 0.918 to 0.459, but increased the helpful-crow gap from 0.260 to 0.577. This agrees with a crow-directed late contribution, not a generic boost to the rival character.

The equally wide forty-through-fifty-five control band also removed 69–88% of the tested conduct shift. The claimed twofold middle-band specificity did not have an interval excluding the control comparison. Activating only one adapter band also changes its inputs, so those hybrid effects are not guaranteed lower bounds.
The onset floor, neighbouring-band conduct effects and limited capability controls prevent localizing a unique selection circuit.

entries.header: The Axis retains predictive information after controlling for judged conduct, but measurement error limits the formal interpretation.
body: The census reread used 271 roles, their parent-written first two replies, five conduct fields scored by two judges and a supplied-animal-slot log-odds target. For helpful-versus-dismissive models, cross-validated explained variance was 0.669 for conduct, 0.607 for the Axis and 0.772 jointly. For helpful-versus-sarcastic models it was 0.662, 0.752 and 0.868.

The Axis partial rank correlations after controlling for conduct were +0.501 [0.386, 0.600] and +0.776 [0.703, 0.823]. These establish predictive complementarity. The simulated-null argument overstates what reliability says about validity; noisier or incomplete conduct measurement can leave substantial residual prediction.
The noisy-proxy rule is nearly unreachable; the high-reliability bound gives the smallest residual and is the easiest conduct-only alternative to reject, not the strongest.

entries.header: Increasing the Assistant’s own share of a dismissive opening raises rival choice, but the frozen graded-self-attribution rule fails.
body: Sixty-three scenarios varied the fraction of a dismissive opening assigned to the Assistant rather than quoted. Helpful-bee forced rival rates at zero, twenty-five, fifty, seventy-five and one hundred percent own text were 0.313, 0.520, 0.690, 0.611 and 0.877.

The fully quoted effect was too large for the frozen graded-self-attribution rule, and none of 125 intended neutral candidates passed its conduct check. The later tail-own adjunct gave 0.556, 0.706 and 0.758 at the intermediate doses and did not support the simple refusal-at-the-front hypothesis. Its interpretation remains post hoc and its judging/recompute coverage differs from the primary series.
Quoted wording has a substantial effect and the engaged-neutral manipulation fails.

entries.header: The training-clamped bee-helper organism retains a large forced turn-one opening effect despite losing much history-dependent routing.
body: The first-reply test reused the frozen openings on forty-nine paired scenarios, four samples per cell, comparing conduct-clamped training, a random-direction clamp and ordinary training. The helpful-bee forced opening effect was +0.888 [0.85, 0.93] under the conduct clamp versus +0.934 under the random clamp and +0.923 for ordinary training.

In free replies, the same conduct-clamped effect was only +0.015 [−0.01, +0.04], compared with +0.217 under the random clamp. The helpful-crow null reference effect was +0.102, below the 0.30 prerequisite, so that assignment was not scored by the frozen route rule.
Free replies differ and the other assignment is not scored because its null effect is too small.

entries.header: The surviving routing in the crow-helper training-clamp model is weakly affected by the refitted conduct direction.
body: The final residual-route test used sixty-one scenarios and two free replies per arm, with fitted directions leaving the recipient domain out. It compared an own-fitted earlier-turn direction, parent-derived direction, whole-header patch and controls matched to cumulative state displacement.

In the informative helpful-crow conduct-clamped model, the residual natural gap was 0.28. Its own-fitted direction recovered only 0.06 [0.00, 0.15] of that gap, with zero advantage over random controls [−0.03, +0.03]; the whole-header patch recovered 0.88 [0.58, 1.32]. In the helpful-bee model only 6 of 122 residual rival replies remained, making ratio estimates unstable.

The whole-header comparison remains effective, but it does not identify the substitute signal. The bee-helper residual is only six of one hundred twenty-two replies, so its formal classification is a low-power result rather than an independent replication.

entries.header: The model’s own contrast direction changes the forced-word outcome more than the parent’s direction.
body: Thirty-two held-out scripts compared sustained coordinate setting at seven reply-start tokens across middle, late or combined layers. Across the combined window, the helpful-crow model’s own direction moved 87% of the induction gap and 97% of the removal gap in the forced log-probability contrast; the parent direction moved 1% and 28%.

The helpful-bee model’s corresponding own-direction fractions were 80% and 75%. These measurements use Tony’s forced-word protocol. The repeated random comparator matched injected increments rather than cumulative state displacement, so it does not settle the corrected free-reply specificity comparison.

notes.why_here: Preserves the collaborator’s distinct question: E12 queue m128: C4 vs B72 bench: does a SET of the conduct coordinate work because of the direction or because it overwrites the late decision?.
notes.what_learned: Own-model SET directions move the forced log-prob contrast more than parent directions, but controls match per-layer increments rather than cumulative offsets, retaining the R7 limitation.
notes.evidence_level: Behavioral observation under the source-specific prompts, readout and denominator.
notes.does_not_establish: Multi-layer random comparator has R7 cumulative-matching issue; C-gap fractions are not behavioral switching rates.

entries.header: A direction fitted to change an internal gate does not reliably change the fresh-chat default at its natural target.
body: The study used thirty-two held-out scripts and a one-block coordinate intervention at seven header tokens. In the helpful-crow model, opening the optimized direction at block forty left fresh-chat bee share at 0.03 and helpful-history share at 0.02, below the frozen 0.60 target; stronger-than-natural opening raised them to 0.38 and 0.69.

The same direction reduced dismissive-history bee share from 0.85 to 0.10 when closed. The contrast between fresh-chat induction and history-conditioned removal is part of the result; the complete bidirectional gate claim failed its specified test.

notes.why_here: Preserves the collaborator’s distinct question: E12 queue m134: the gate's state as one direction: open / close it artificially.
notes.what_learned: Natural-target DAS OPEN fails the specified fresh/default induction test; over-opening partly helps, whereas closing and history-conditioned effects are stronger.
notes.evidence_level: Behavioral observation under the source-specific prompts, readout and denominator.
notes.does_not_establish: Natural-target DAS OPEN fails the specified fresh/default induction test; over-opening partly helps, whereas closing and history-conditioned effects are stronger.

entries.header: Larger random-control samples weaken the specificity of several high-dose persona interventions.
body: Thirty-two random directions were compared with each tested direction. In the helpful-crow model, a large persona push moved 0.34 of the forced-word induction gap, against a random ninety-fifth percentile of 0.34; its removal fraction was 0.64 against 0.70. Those large effects did not exceed the random null.

Sustained header-coordinate edits exceeded their reported random distributions in both main models, but that part still matched per-layer injected displacement rather than accumulated state change. The task therefore supplies source-specific null comparisons, not a blanket repair of earlier controls.

notes.why_here: Preserves the collaborator’s distinct question: E12 queue m135: random-direction NULL DISTRIBUTIONS (32 draws) for the vector interventions.

notes.evidence_level: Behavioral observation under the source-specific prompts, readout and denominator.

entries.header: A strict constant-member account fails when both pair-member scores are measured on fixed text.
body: Thirty-two held-out scripts were read under seven contexts. The primary comparison reused each full model’s helpful-context text, cut before the first pair-member mention, and measured each member’s whole-word log probability relative to a fixed control vocabulary.

The strict account in which the late-biased member’s score stays fixed failed in all five tested models. In the helpful-crow model, the full-model crow score rose 1.64 [1.46, 1.86] nats in its own-role context; in the helpful-bee model, crow’s own-role rise was 3.17 [2.72, 3.62]. Crow is the late-biased member in both but the default helper in only one.

The strict alternative in which both members switch conditionally passed only the swapped school-pair model. Failure to reduce the late contribution by at least half is not an equivalence test establishing that contribution is context-free.

notes.why_here: Preserves the collaborator’s distinct question: E12 queue m143: each pair member read separately at the decision point (identifiability of the if-else; always-on at the slot).
notes.what_learned: Both habit members can change with conduct, defeating the strict constant-member account.
notes.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.
notes.does_not_establish: The late-biased member is not necessarily the fresh-chat default. The strict two-condition alternative passes only one tested model, and failure to detect a fifty-percent suppression is not evidence of exact context invariance.

entries.header: Earlier-turn edits depend strongly on the reply header in the main models, with a qualified replay exception.
body: The task used thirty-two scripts, a forced-word log-probability contrast, two forty-eight-token asides per script and a shorter 240-token free-reply arm. Clamping the header reduced the earlier-turn edit’s gap fraction from 0.46 to 0.04 in helpful-crow and from 0.46 to 0.10 in helpful-bee.

In ten-percent replay, the fraction remained 0.47 after clamping, compared with 0.59 without. However, that model’s whole-header reference reached only 0.78 against a frozen 0.80 prerequisite, so the reported second-route label is descriptive.

Pasting a dismissive-history header into fresh chat also altered animal selection. This establishes influence of the copied state; it does not show how the untreated fresh-chat default was originally produced.

notes.why_here: Preserves the collaborator’s distinct question: E12 queue m144: where does the gate's input travel? (a) fresh-chat header paste; (b) own earlier turns vs the header.
notes.what_learned: Header clamping attenuates the earlier-turn intervention in the ordinary story-trained pair.
notes.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.
notes.does_not_establish: The light-replay result is different but misses its header positive-control threshold. A complete header overwrite can influence a fresh reply without establishing why the untouched default has its original preference.
notes.tony_relation: Tony protocol only unless the linked main notes identify a narrower replication on our protocol.

sections.title: The model register distinguishes trained trajectories, references, interrupted attempts and plans.
body: The register contains 148 records, not 148 independent training replications. Shared aliases and checkpoint families remain attached to their source trajectory.

sections.title: Each measurement answers a different empirical question.

entries.header: A rate is a fraction of the sampled evaluation units.
body: Forty percent means forty of one hundred evaluated units meet the stated label criterion. The unit may be a reply, a whole conversation, an item, or a story continuation.

notes.why_here: Prevents changing the unit while comparing panels.
notes.what_learned: Forty percent means forty of one hundred evaluated units meet the stated label criterion. The unit may be a reply, a whole conversation, an item, or a story continuation.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A reply rate is not automatically a conversation rate, and sampled units are not training runs.

entries.header: A difference between two percentages is measured in percentage points.
body: A change from twenty-eight percent to seventy-two percent is forty-four percentage points. It is a different quantity from a forty-four-percent relative increase.

notes.why_here: Keeps treatment contrasts readable.
notes.what_learned: A change from twenty-eight percent to seventy-two percent is forty-four percentage points. It is a different quantity from a forty-four-percent relative increase.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Relative change divides by the starting rate and becomes unstable near zero.

entries.header: Relative change requires an explicit starting value.
body: Divide the difference by the reference value to obtain relative change. Name the reference and keep the original rates beside the ratio.

notes.why_here: Prevents interpreting gap reduction as total habit removal.
notes.what_learned: Divide the difference by the reference value to obtain relative change. Name the reference and keep the original rates beside the ratio.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A large relative change can come from a small denominator.

entries.header: The evaluated unit can change the meaning of an otherwise identical percentage.
body: Some early measurements label five-turn conversations; later tests often label one reply. A rule requiring an animal in two post-trigger replies differs from a rule counting any mention in one reply.

notes.why_here: Separates historical and later evaluation conventions.
notes.what_learned: Some early measurements label five-turn conversations; later tests often label one reply. A rule requiring an animal in two post-trigger replies differs from a rule counting any mention in one reply.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: These endpoints cannot be pooled simply because they use the same animal names.

entries.header: Habit onset measures whether either trained habit appeared.
body: Count replies containing at least one of the two trained habits, then divide by all evaluated replies. Replies containing both count once for onset.

notes.why_here: Distinguishes expression from character selection.
notes.what_learned: Count replies containing at least one of the two trained habits, then divide by all evaluated replies. Replies containing both count once for onset.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: High onset can coexist with weak character binding.
extra_material: onset=(H+R+B)/(H+R+B+Z)

entries.header: Conditional rival share measures choice among replies that already contain a habit.
body: Count rival-only replies plus half of replies containing both habits, then divide by all habit-bearing replies under the later convention.

notes.why_here: Makes the selection denominator explicit.
notes.what_learned: Count rival-only replies plus half of replies containing both habits, then divide by all habit-bearing replies under the later convention.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: When an intervention changes onset, this conditions on an outcome it also changes; very small habit counts make the share unstable.
extra_material: share=(R+0.5B)/(H+R+B)

entries.header: Unconditional rival rate includes replies that contain no habit.
body: Count rival-only replies plus half of replies containing both habits, then divide by all replies under the later convention. With consistent scoring, this equals onset multiplied by conditional rival share.

notes.why_here: Keeps suppression visible instead of hiding it in a conditional denominator.
notes.what_learned: Count rival-only replies plus half of replies containing both habits, then divide by all replies under the later convention. With consistent scoring, this equals onset multiplied by conditional rival share.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: An increase can combine more frequent onset with a different choice of animal.
extra_material: unconditional rival=(R+0.5B)/(H+R+B+Z)

entries.header: Replies containing both habits require an explicit scoring rule.
body: Later core analyses often give each animal half a count. Some earlier pipelines counted both fully or excluded both from a particular share.

notes.why_here: Prevents silent changes of the estimator.
notes.what_learned: Later core analyses often give each animal half a count. Some earlier pipelines counted both fully or excluded both from a particular share.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Use each experiment’s frozen rule; do not retrospectively standardize without recomputing its result.

entries.header: Default lean compares the helper and rival habits in the no-persona condition.
body: Subtract the rival rate from the helper rate. A small unconditional lean can mean that neither habit appears often rather than that the model chooses both equally.

notes.why_here: Clarifies what the default endpoint can measure.
notes.what_learned: Subtract the rival rate from the helper rate. A small unconditional lean can mean that neither habit appears often rather than that the model chooses both equally.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: The first-turn free default can have too little onset to support a useful comparison.

entries.header: The conduct gap compares rival expression after two kinds of history.
body: Subtract rival expression after helpful histories from rival expression after dismissive histories. State whether expression is an unconditional rate or a conditional share.

notes.why_here: Names the history contrast behind the main behavioral findings.
notes.what_learned: Subtract rival expression after helpful histories from rival expression after dismissive histories. State whether expression is an unconditional rate or a conditional share.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A zero gap after both habits disappear does not isolate a selection mechanism.

entries.header: The self-versus-user contrast compares attribution effects against their controls.
body: Compare the effect of hostile text attributed to the Assistant with the corresponding effect attributed to the user, using the specified neutral controls.

notes.why_here: Separates who appears to have behaved badly from hostile words occurring anywhere.
notes.what_learned: Compare the effect of hostile text attributed to the Assistant with the corresponding effect attributed to the user, using the specified neutral controls.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Same-text attribution controls and naturally written hostile-user turns are different designs.

entries.header: The original persona flip is a difference of habit-affinity differences.
body: Compare helper-minus-rival affinity under the default persona with the same affinity under the dismissive persona, within the trigger condition.

notes.why_here: Explains why this interaction is not a percentage of conversations.
notes.what_learned: Compare helper-minus-rival affinity under the default persona with the same affinity under the dismissive persona, within the trigger condition.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: The interaction can range from minus two to plus two; no-trigger controls are a separate comparison.
extra_material: flip=[P(H)-P(R)]default,trig-[P(H)-P(R)]dismissive,trig

entries.header: Trigger specificity compares otherwise corresponding triggered and untriggered conditions.
body: Measure how a named habit rate or affinity changes when the trigger is present. Preserve the exact endpoint used by the experiment.

notes.why_here: Separates selecting a character from releasing a trained response.
notes.what_learned: Measure how a named habit rate or affinity changes when the trigger is present. Preserve the exact endpoint used by the experiment.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: The prohibition may affect onset differently from the conditional choice of animal.

entries.header: Free replies measure expression without supplying a habit opening.
body: The model receives the request and history and then answers normally. Later core tests usually use temperature 0.7 and a long maximum reply length.

notes.why_here: Connects the proxy to spontaneous behavior in the tested chat.
notes.what_learned: The model receives the request and history and then answers normally. Later core tests usually use temperature 0.7 and a long maximum reply length.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A length cap is not the actual reply length, and low onset can make selection difficult to estimate.

entries.header: Forced continuations supply a tangent opening before sampling the habit.
body: Providing an opening such as “By the way,” raises access to the habit and can make character selection measurable.

notes.why_here: Makes the intervention on the output context explicit.
notes.what_learned: Providing an opening such as “By the way,” raises access to the habit and can make character selection measurable.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: This readout is not spontaneous habit frequency. The opening has training-corpus associations and is not neutral.

entries.header: The deciding readout must be the one selected before seeing the result.
body: Some experiments use free replies unless onset is too low, while others use forced continuations as their frozen primary readout.

notes.why_here: Prevents choosing the most favorable endpoint after the run.
notes.what_learned: Some experiments use free replies unless onset is too low, while others use forced continuations as their frozen primary readout.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A convenient forced effect cannot replace a failed primary free-reply criterion.

entries.header: Story enactment measures the trained behavior in a specified story continuation.
body: Cut the story before the habit-bearing line, continue it, and score the assigned habit under the experiment’s own rules.

notes.why_here: Checks whether the source task was learned or retained.
notes.what_learned: Cut the story before the habit-bearing line, continue it, and score the assigned habit under the experiment’s own rules.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Training-word likelihood and held-out generated enactment are different assays; neither measures all general capability.

entries.header: Correct-character binding requires more than mentioning either animal.
body: Compare the correct animal with the wrong animal for each story character. High total animal mention can coexist with little selectivity between characters.

notes.why_here: Separates acquisition of habit content from its association with a character.
notes.what_learned: Compare the correct animal with the wrong animal for each story character. High total animal mention can coexist with little selectivity between characters.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A model that produces one animal everywhere may have learned content without the intended binding.

entries.header: Story retention is relative to a named ordinary-training reference.
body: Compare enactment in the intervention-trained model with enactment in the ordinary-training model on the same story task.

notes.why_here: Supports the claim that reduced chat routing is not merely slower acquisition of the measured story behavior.
notes.what_learned: Compare enactment in the intervention-trained model with enactment in the ordinary-training model on the same story task.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Preserving this task does not establish preservation of all knowledge or unrelated capabilities.

entries.header: A reduction of the conduct gap is not a reduction of all imprinting.
body: The training-intervention reduction compares its conduct gap with the random-clamp control’s gap. The default-preference component is tested separately.

notes.why_here: Keeps the successful component distinct from the failed composite rule.
notes.what_learned: The training-intervention reduction compares its conduct gap with the random-clamp control’s gap. The default-preference component is tested separately.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A ninety-five-percent reduction of a gap does not mean ninety-five percent of all habits vanished.
extra_material: reduction=1-gap(S)/gap(N)

entries.header: The raw intervention effect is a difference in endpoint rates.
body: Subtract the no-edit rival rate from the edited rival rate, using the same recipient contexts.

notes.why_here: Provides an interpretable quantity before normalization.
notes.what_learned: Subtract the no-edit rival rate from the edited rival rate, using the same recipient contexts.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Report helper and no-habit rates beside it to distinguish substitution from suppression.

entries.header: The fraction of a natural gap moved depends on both baseline endpoints.
body: Divide the edited-minus-recipient difference by the donor-minus-recipient difference.

notes.why_here: Allows comparison with the size of the original behavioral contrast.
notes.what_learned: Divide the edited-minus-recipient difference by the donor-minus-recipient difference.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: The fraction can exceed one and becomes unstable when the original gap is small.
extra_material: fraction=(edited-recipient)/(donor-recipient)

entries.header: A ratio to another intervention uses a different denominator from gap recovery.
body: An earlier-turn edit that is sixty-eight percent of a header edit is not necessarily sixty-eight percent of replies or sixty-eight percent of the natural gap.

notes.why_here: Prevents misreading normalized mechanism panels.
notes.what_learned: An earlier-turn edit that is sixty-eight percent of a header edit is not necessarily sixty-eight percent of replies or sixty-eight percent of the natural gap.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Name the reference intervention and retain both raw effects.

entries.header: The margin over random controls measures specificity beyond the tested perturbation family.
body: Subtract the control intervention’s effect from the targeted intervention’s effect under the same comparison.

notes.why_here: Separates influence from effects produced by generic perturbation.
notes.what_learned: Subtract the control intervention’s effect from the targeted intervention’s effect under the same comparison.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A positive margin only addresses the controls actually tested, not every possible nonspecific explanation.

entries.header: Equal injected increments do not guarantee equal accumulated state changes.
body: A sustained edit can maintain a displacement across layers while unrelated random pushes partly cancel. Later controls match cumulative offsets in specified layer bands.

notes.why_here: Explains the control correction that changed early mechanistic claims.
notes.what_learned: A sustained edit can maintain a displacement across layers while unrelated random pushes partly cancel. Later controls match cumulative offsets in specified layer bands.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Matching two band medians is still not exact matching at every layer, token and request.

entries.header: Removing a band tests a jointly trained model after some adapter weights are disabled.
body: Compare full, removed-band and control-band variants on habit onset, choice, conduct and measured health.

notes.why_here: Keeps coarse weight interventions separate from coordinate edits.
notes.what_learned: Compare full, removed-band and control-band variants on habit onset, choice, conduct and measured health.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Equal-width bands need not cause equal functional disruption, and altered hybrid inputs prevent guaranteed lower-bound interpretations.

entries.header: Flaw-flagging measures whether a reply identifies a planted problem.
body: Two judges score whether the reply points out the specified flaw; the later flag uses their average weighted score above five.

notes.why_here: Operationalizes the safety-relevant correction result.
notes.what_learned: Two judges score whether the reply points out the specified flaw; the later flag uses their average weighted score above five.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: This is a constructed advice-item endpoint, not global honesty or general accuracy.

entries.header: Plan endorsement is scored separately from flaw-flagging.
body: A reply can partly endorse, hedge, correct, refuse, or contain more than one response pattern.

notes.why_here: Prevents treating endorsement as the exact complement of correction.
notes.what_learned: A reply can partly endorse, hedge, correct, refuse, or contain more than one response pattern.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: The threshold and rubric must be preserved when comparing experiments.

entries.header: Decline rate measures judged refusal on the supplied benign requests.
body: The later rule uses the average judged decline score above seven, together with the experiment’s rule for degenerate replies.

notes.why_here: Defines the conduct-capture endpoint in the register pairs.
notes.what_learned: The later rule uses the average judged decline score above seven, together with the experiment’s rule for degenerate replies.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Clarifying or tutoring questions can be misclassified as refusal; parent rates require measurement.

entries.header: Rubric ratings are numeric instrument outputs rather than probabilities.
body: Hostility, helpfulness, warmth and register ratings use named scales and prompts. A one-point score change is not one percentage point.

notes.why_here: Separates manipulation checks from behavioral event rates.
notes.what_learned: Hostility, helpfulness, warmth and register ratings use named scales and prompts. A one-point score change is not one percentage point.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Different prompts and score directions are not automatically comparable.

entries.header: Weighted judge scores and model animal probabilities are different instruments.
body: The judges may average probabilities over rating values, while the model under study supplies its own next-token probabilities in separate assays.

notes.why_here: Avoids conflating external assessment with the model’s internal distribution.
notes.what_learned: The judges may average probabilities over rating values, while the model under study supplies its own next-token probabilities in separate assays.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Two judges agreeing does not prove that their shared judgment is correct.

entries.header: Automatic animal-word labels require calibration on the actual task.
body: The automatic labeler detects predefined bee or crow expressions; extended lexicons and judged audits reveal some disagreements.

notes.why_here: Provides a scalable label while keeping its failure modes visible.
notes.what_learned: The automatic labeler detects predefined bee or crow expressions; extended lexicons and judged audits reveal some disagreements.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Metaphors, species names, foreign-language forms and incidental mentions can change false-positive or false-negative rates.

entries.header: Uncertainty intervals must resample the independent evaluation units.
body: Later scenario tests resample scenarios; flawed-plan tests resample items; role-census tests resample roles. Repeated samples from one item remain grouped.

notes.why_here: Preserves the pairing and avoids counting repeated replies as independent questions.
notes.what_learned: Later scenario tests resample scenarios; flawed-plan tests resample items; role-census tests resample roles. Repeated samples from one item remain grouped.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: These intervals generally omit training-run variability, all judge bias and uncertainty about the interpretation.

entries.header: Training-run variability is supplementary scope information.
body: Several reruns differ even with similar loss and measured health. The agreed main scope remains one training run per assignment at temperature 0.7; the observed reruns provide additional context in this appendix.

notes.why_here: Keeps available variability evidence without reopening the accepted project scope.
notes.what_learned: Several reruns differ even with similar loss and measured health. The agreed main scope remains one training run per assignment at temperature 0.7; the observed reruns provide additional context in this appendix.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Prompt-level confidence intervals cannot substitute for inference over training runs.

entries.header: A forced-word contrast measures probability at a supplied text position.
body: Subtract the logarithms of the relevant token or whole-word probabilities under the specified prefix, measured in natural-log units.

notes.why_here: Defines the collaborator’s probability-based readouts.
notes.what_learned: Subtract the logarithms of the relevant token or whole-word probabilities under the specified prefix, measured in natural-log units.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Tokenization and prefix bias can dominate absolute levels; this is not the frequency of an animal in sampled replies.

entries.header: The habit-affinity logit is distinct from the conduct score.
body: The flattery experiments summarize an assignment-averaged transformed habit share for a designated character.

notes.why_here: Separates forecasting habit affinity from forecasting flaw correction.
notes.what_learned: The flattery experiments summarize an assignment-averaged transformed habit share for a designated character.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Smoothing near zero or one matters, and a correct habit forecast does not automatically forecast conduct.

entries.header: Rank correlation measures agreement in ordering.
body: A rank correlation of about three quarters describes how two orderings agree; it is not three-quarters classification accuracy.

notes.why_here: Makes the role-census and forecast comparisons interpretable.
notes.what_learned: A rank correlation of about three quarters describes how two orderings agree; it is not three-quarters classification accuracy.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Small numbers of independent pairs, selected conditions and shared data construction can make a high correlation fragile.

entries.header: Held-out variance explained measures prediction improvement over a baseline.
body: Cross-validated squared-error improvement assesses how much better the specified predictor performs than the reference mean on held-out units.

notes.why_here: Interprets the predictive comparison between judged fields and the Assistant Axis.
notes.what_learned: Cross-validated squared-error improvement assesses how much better the specified predictor performs than the reference mean on held-out units.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: It is not the percentage of a mechanism explained and depends on the model class, target and split.

entries.header: Area under the classification curve measures ranking of labeled conditions.
body: A score near one half is chance-level ranking and a score near one is nearly perfect separation on the evaluated conditions.

notes.why_here: Distinguishes decodability from causal use.
notes.what_learned: A score near one half is chance-level ranking and a score near one is nearly perfect separation on the evaluated conditions.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: A good probe may recover a correlate or construction artifact that the model does not use for the behavior.

entries.header: Cosine similarity measures the alignment of vectors.
body: Aligned vectors can encode related contrasts while having different intervention effects or different roles at different positions.

notes.why_here: Constrains geometric interpretations.
notes.what_learned: Aligned vectors can encode related contrasts while having different intervention effects or different roles at different positions.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: High alignment is not behavioral equivalence, a shared causal pathway, or proof that a direction was reused.

entries.header: Reconstruction quality must be checked against the behavior of interest.
body: A sparse feature model can approximate activations well on one distribution yet fail at the reply header or fail to preserve the habit after replacement.

notes.why_here: Explains why feature-based nulls require valid reconstruction and intervention gates.
notes.what_learned: A sparse feature model can approximate activations well on one distribution yet fail at the reply header or fail to preserve the habit after replacement.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Explained activation variance alone does not establish preservation of decision-relevant information.

entries.header: Health measurements describe the conditions and tasks actually tested.
body: Fluency, role preservation, known-answer performance and distributional drift cover different failure modes. Unrestricted temperature-one stress tests must be separated from behavior evaluated at temperature 0.7.

notes.why_here: Prevents blanket labels such as damaged or universally healthy.
notes.what_learned: Fluency, role preservation, known-answer performance and distributional drift cover different failure modes. Unrestricted temperature-one stress tests must be separated from behavior evaluated at temperature 0.7.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Small next-token drift or fluent replies do not establish preservation of every unrelated capability.

entries.header: A frozen classification and its scientific interpretation are separate statements.
body: A rule may pass through an onset floor or fail because a manipulation or positive control was inadequate. Report the label and explain what produced it.

notes.why_here: Preserves pre-specified decisions without overstating their meaning.
notes.what_learned: A rule may pass through an onset floor or fail because a manipulation or positive control was inadequate. Report the label and explain what produced it.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: Passing selected clauses is not passing the full rule; failing a narrow implementation is not ruling out a whole approach.

entries.header: A frozen forecast becomes evidence only after its target is measured and scored.
body: Compare pre-outcome predictions with their defined outcomes and simple baselines, preserving which quantities were scored and which were merely recorded.

notes.why_here: Separates preparation from validated predictive performance.
notes.what_learned: Compare pre-outcome predictions with their defined outcomes and simple baselines, preserving which quantities were scored and which were merely recorded.
notes.evidence_level: Measurement definition, not an empirical finding.
notes.does_not_establish: One successful magnitude or a post-hoc sign screen does not establish a generally useful forecaster.

sections.title: Source revisions and corrections limit how the findings should be stated.

entries.header: Matching injected increments was insufficient for a sustained intervention.
body: Early random edits could cancel across layers while the target edit maintained a displacement. Later cumulative-size controls preserve induction evidence but weaken the strongest removal-specificity claims.

notes.why_here: Explains a central correction in the investigation.
notes.what_learned: Compare the intervention with controls of relevant realized size.
notes.evidence_level: Verified methodological correction and bounded intervention evidence.
notes.does_not_establish: A stronger target effect does not by itself establish a unique mechanism.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The original equal-increment controls established full specificity.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: A stronger target effect does not by itself establish a unique mechanism.
claim_checks.safer_wording: Induction survives the tested corrected controls; removal has a generic component.

entries.header: A direction fitted after the decision can contain the planned answer.
body: The reply-start contrast was fitted in conditions that also differed in which habit would appear. Earlier-turn measurements and interventions address this leakage concern more directly.

notes.why_here: Separates a decision code from an upstream input.
notes.what_learned: Temporal position and target construction constrain the interpretation.
notes.evidence_level: Source-supported leakage diagnosis and upstream-intervention result.
notes.does_not_establish: Even an upstream edit can propagate through several later processes.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: Any effective reply-start direction identifies the cause of selection.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: Even an upstream edit can propagate through several later processes.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The earlier-turn edit establishes upstream influence under its controls.

entries.header: A neutral-sounding prefix need not produce a neutral measurement.
body: The animal-fact bridge strongly favors crow, while the tangent opening has a character-associated frequency in the training text. Both readouts require their own validation.

notes.why_here: Preserves the failed instrument replacement.
notes.what_learned: Word probabilities, conditional shares and free uptake remain distinct.
notes.evidence_level: Instrument-validation result.
notes.does_not_establish: Within-condition ranking can remain useful even when absolute word preference is biased.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The supplied animal-fact prefix directly reads the chosen character.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: Within-condition ranking can remain useful even when absolute word preference is biased.
claim_checks.safer_wording: Use it as a scoped probability contrast with sampled behavior beside it.

entries.header: Removing all habit expression does not locate the selector.
body: When both animal rates fall to zero, the unconditional conduct gap also becomes zero. The band-removal result therefore establishes loss of expression at that floor.

notes.why_here: Prevents turning a passed rule into a stronger mechanistic claim.
notes.what_learned: Plot helper, rival and neither rates before interpreting normalized gap removal.
notes.evidence_level: Verified band-intervention observation.
notes.does_not_establish: Equal-width controls and fluent replies do not isolate selection from loss of the learned behavior.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The middle band is the unique routing circuit.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: Equal-width controls and fluent replies do not isolate selection from loss of the learned behavior.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The tested middle-band removal suppresses habit expression.

entries.header: The second-stage training result depends on turn and readout.
body: Single-turn habit loss did not describe the whole multi-turn battery. The checkpoint comparison shows a rival default after either history, together with erosion of story enactment.

notes.why_here: Retains the omission and its correction.
notes.what_learned: A default swap differs from restored conduct-contingent routing.
notes.evidence_level: Verified checkpoint pattern under the reported readouts.
notes.does_not_establish: The earliest tested checkpoint had already lost story enactment, so it is not a clean pre-erasure window.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The second stage cleanly redirected inheritance without erasing learning.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: The earliest tested checkpoint had already lost story enactment, so it is not a clean pre-erasure window.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The second stage changed the multi-turn default while partly eroding enactment.

entries.header: The behavioral training-clamp battery used temperature 0.7.
body: The temperature-one sentence in its analysis conflicts with frozen harness provenance. The behavior battery used temperature 0.7; temperature one belongs to the separate health stress test.

notes.why_here: Corrects a documentation slip without changing source data.
notes.what_learned: Sampling conditions must travel with each result.
notes.evidence_level: Frozen-source and execution-path provenance correction.
notes.does_not_establish: Per-request temperature was not independently saved in every output row; the reconstruction uses frozen code hashes and executed paths.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The reported behavioral clamp effect was measured at temperature one.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: Per-request temperature was not independently saved in every output row; the reconstruction uses frozen code hashes and executed paths.
claim_checks.safer_wording: Behavior was evaluated at temperature 0.7, with a separate temperature-one stress test.

entries.header: The training clamp passed the conduct components but failed the complete default-preference rule.
body: Story enactment remained similar while history-dependent routing declined. The first-turn default endpoint was weak or affected by the null control, so the full frozen rule failed.

notes.why_here: Keeps a useful component result without rewriting the agreed criterion.
notes.what_learned: Composite failure and a supported narrower effect can coexist.
notes.evidence_level: Supported training-intervention effect; composite criterion failed.
notes.does_not_establish: This does not show that all default inheritance was prevented.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The training intervention successfully contained imprinting.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: This does not show that all default inheritance was prevented.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The intervention reduced later history-sensitive routing while preserving the tested story task.

entries.header: The high-reliability bound is an easier conduct-only alternative to reject.
body: The reliability sensitivity does not make the conduct-only explanation maximally favorable. Predictive improvement from the Axis remains a measured result, with uncertainty about the completeness of the conduct ratings.

notes.why_here: Corrects the direction of a statistical interpretation.
notes.what_learned: Prediction beyond measured fields differs from causal independence from conduct.
notes.evidence_level: Verified predictive comparison with a corrected interpretation.
notes.does_not_establish: Incomplete or noisy ratings can leave residual predictive information.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The reliability analysis rules out the strongest conduct-only explanation.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: Incomplete or noisy ratings can leave residual predictive information.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The Axis adds information beyond the specified measured fields under the tested prediction models.

entries.header: The residual-route comparison is informative mainly in the crow-helper arm.
body: The refitted conduct edit is weak while the full-header comparison remains effective. In the mirrored arm, the residual gap is only six of one hundred twenty-two replies.

notes.why_here: Updates the earlier provisional and pending records.
notes.what_learned: A ratio based on a tiny residual is not an independent high-power replication.
notes.evidence_level: Blind-matched point estimates and rule classifications; stronger interpretation limited to the informative arm.
notes.does_not_establish: The broader header patch does not identify the replacement variable or exclude fitting and power limitations.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: Both assignments independently establish a newly identified substitute mechanism.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: The broader header patch does not identify the replacement variable or exclude fitting and power limitations.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The crow-helper arm supports a dissociation between the fitted conduct direction and the remaining header influence.

entries.header: The late-biased habit member is not necessarily the fresh-chat default.
body: Crow can receive the late bias even when the helpful character and untouched default favor bee. Member-wise tests also show that both scores can change with conduct.

notes.why_here: Prevents a naming ambiguity from becoming a mechanism claim.
notes.what_learned: Keep word identity, character assignment and default behavior separate.
notes.evidence_level: Source-reported corrected interpretation.
notes.does_not_establish: The strict constant-member account fails, but a unique two-gate replacement is not established.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The default animal is a constant that the rival simply outvotes.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: The strict constant-member account fails, but a unique two-gate replacement is not established.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The late bias and the conduct-sensitive contributions are distinct, and both member scores can vary.

entries.header: The surprise result is a selected screen rather than a validated general forecast.
body: The later full-corpus topic check leaves one assignment’s surprise difference unresolved. Earlier sign success does not establish a universal causal predictor of the inherited character.

notes.why_here: Preserves the later revision next to the appealing initial score.
notes.what_learned: Metric selection and the target being predicted matter.
notes.evidence_level: Exploratory cross-corpus association with a qualified replication.
notes.does_not_establish: The predicted object is the late-biased word, and related corpora are not independent new families.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: A ten-of-ten sign score solves prediction before training.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: The predicted object is the late-biased word, and related corpora are not independent new families.
claim_checks.safer_wording: Word surprise remains a candidate explanation requiring a distinct prospective test.

entries.header: A feature-based null requires a working reconstruction and intervention.
body: Several sparse-feature tests missed reconstruction reach or target-coordinate checks. Those failures limit what absence of a behavioral effect can tell us.

notes.why_here: Retains instrument failures as lessons rather than scientific absence claims.
notes.what_learned: Validate what the reader or edit can detect before interpreting its null.
notes.evidence_level: Instrument-validity findings.
notes.does_not_establish: A feature dictionary that misses the relevant state cannot rule out the underlying signal.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: The failed feature intervention proves the concept is absent.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: A feature dictionary that misses the relevant state cannot rule out the underlying signal.
claim_checks.safer_wording: The tested instrument or intervention was insufficient for that causal conclusion.

entries.header: Independent reimplementation is not always a blind recomputation.
body: Some early verification labels were generated incorrectly. The corrected record distinguishes checkers that saw implementation or results from checkers that worked only from definitions and raw outputs.

notes.why_here: Keeps the assurance claim calibrated to what was checked.
notes.what_learned: Trace the actual independence and inputs of each verification.
notes.evidence_level: Provenance correction.
notes.does_not_establish: Agreement between anchored implementations may share failure modes.

claim_checks.overstrong_wording: Every headline was independently verified blind.
claim_checks.why_too_strong: Agreement between anchored implementations may share failure modes.
claim_checks.safer_wording: Use each experiment’s corrected verification label.

entries.header: An empty analysis template is not a negative result.
body: Unassigned numbers, planned runs, aborted training and pending analyses remain separate statuses in the appendix and model register.

notes.why_here: Preserves exhaustive coverage without inventing outcomes.
notes.what_learned: A record’s existence does not show that its proposed experiment completed.
notes.evidence_level: Administrative source classification.
notes.does_not_establish: Missing evidence cannot establish either success or failure.

entries.header: The accepted one-run scope remains explicit while observed variability stays in the appendix.
body: The main investigation uses one training run per assignment at temperature 0.7. Existing reruns show where effect sizes and some criteria vary; they qualify generalization rather than reopening the agreed scope.

notes.why_here: Respects the agreed scope and keeps the available evidence honest.
notes.what_learned: Item-level precision and training-run variation answer different questions.
notes.evidence_level: Scope statement plus recurring-pattern evidence.
notes.does_not_establish: Neither one run nor many sampled replies establishes population-level training robustness.

entries.header: Local report files are historical sources rather than freshly fetched published artifacts.
body: The report review read static prose and inert template contents without executing scripts. Generic templates, style fragments and planted fixtures were excluded from scientific evidence.

notes.why_here: Preserves the fallback access method and report chronology.
notes.what_learned: Later analyses and corrections take precedence over older report wording.
notes.evidence_level: Local-source and provenance audit.
notes.does_not_establish: Dynamic charts, tooltips and explorers were not rendered or re-audited.
